text:
Across from your $shipOrFleet a trio of strange vessels wait, unnaturally motionless. Although they present some features common to all vessels, the designs are in aggregate unlike anything recorded.

Your sensors officer reports that they seem entirely unaffected by the irradiative forces of the nearby red pulsar, radiation seems to slide off of their hull like water. Periodically they disappear and then reappear in place, strangely, readings suggest the vessels are not diving into phase space and they visually have no external phase coils or other markings of phase capable craft. 

Your bridge crew murmurs speculation between their stations about how exactly this is possible, but it is all frivolous without any hard data on the capabilities of the enemy.

A final terrific explosion blanks the external visual pickups. A few seconds later, backups are extruded through the hull.

text:
A final terrific explosion blanks the external visual pickups. A few seconds later, backups are extruded through the hull.

Your sensors officer reports in a hushed voice that no escape pods were detected leaving any of the ships at any point.
Two of the strange vessels were shattered beyond recognition in the fighting, but the third, dormant, now drifts somewhat intact through space.

Your salvage team docks a shuttle at the only entry point along the ships hull, just beneath what appears from external readings to be the bridge. Given no escape pods were launched, a contingent of marines have been assigned to escort the salvor crew incase of hostile action.

After a few tense minutes, reports start to come in. Ominously, the crew of the vessel is nowhere to be found, neither are any signs that anyone ever inhabited the ship. The crew quarters have no amenities or personal affects, and the central datacore has been reduced to slag by an automated sabotage system. 

The majority of the hull's volume is seemingly inaccessible to the intended human crew, but portable scanners reveal it is wormed with the thin conduits and ducts emblematic of an automated maintenance system. While the vessel is heavily damaged and immensely exotic in design, it is theoretically recoverable if we can restore the maintenance drones.

A comms link from your chief engineer appears on your datapad. Likely ready to discuss that very prospect.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam, it seems your intuition was correct. While our data on the fractal vessels we encountered defending the Coronal Hypershunt is limited, this ship is clearly of the same design language, at least superficially. Of course the hull is made of an entirely different material, and this new substance seemingly does not possess the ability to reform like the previous ships." They stop, thinking. 

"Captain, if I may speak plainly. This ship is strange, stranger than anything we've seen so far." They clear their throat and look at you, deadly serious, "it makes an odd number of concessions to human habitation for a ship designed presumably by and for an AI, too many for it to make sense. There is an AI housing onboard, but its hollowed out, a perfect sphere appears to have been removed from the centre to extract the core. Something happened to this ship, I don't think whatever was flying it against us is the same entity that built it."

"The hull is made of an entirely novel material, what exactly it is I'm not yet sure, but initial readings indicate it has fascinating properties." They stop, thinking. 

"But there's something else, Captain. If I may speak plainly. This ship is strange." They clear their throat and look at you, deadly serious, "There is an AI housing onboard, but its hollowed out, a perfect sphere appears to have been removed from the centre to extract the core. If this ship was designed for an AI, it makes an odd number of concessions to human habitation, too many for it to make sense. Something happened to this ship, I don't think whatever was flying it against us is the same entity that built it."

Your chief engineer clears their throat again, then continues "Anyway. I think I can get the maintenance systems working, I don't know who built this ship, or why, but it should be fit to fly. If you want my professional opinion, we should investigate the planet in system too," they look to the side, likely checking a map of the system, "Maddie." 

"Regardless, should we proceed with recovery?"

The connection request hangs for some time before an immense wave of holo-noise floods through the main display, generating thousands of error codes. 

Your comms officer works their console in consternation, it comes to mind that the opposing fleet have seemingly overloaded your comms system with thousands of requests at once. From visual inspection, none of the vessels have the hardware necessary to accomplish such a feat within a reasonable timeframe.

The presence of the hostile fleet nearby in system makes launching a survey expedition inadvisable. If we were to be engaged in combat while supporting ongoing surface operations our tactical options would be greatly diminished.

An initial scan of the surface immediately reveals something immensely strange. Your sensors officer reports that the lidar used for basic geographic mapping returned from the surface much quicker than should be possible, this suggests that something relativistically strange is occurring on the surface.

A drone equipped with an atomic clock, a standard tool in the surveying toolkit, is deployed to the surface and programmed to return a signal in exactly one hour. Minutes later, a signal is received by your comms officer. There is only one conclusion, time progresses much faster on the surface of Maddie than here in orbit,

Naturally, most of your crew are unnerved by the prospect of a surface expedition to such a world. Many spacer horror stories feature relativity as an antagonist, an invisible but inexorable force that pushes people apart by stretching the time between them.

text:
Your $shipOrFleet maintains a safe distance from Maddie. Given the strange relativity effects of this world your operations chief has advised staying off of the surface, especially now we have obtained a modest sample of the frictionless material. 

None of the crew seem particularly eager to return to the planet regardless, given the way it aged the previous team over a cycle within hours.

After extensive preparation (and reiteration of the hazard pay policy) a volunteer survey team is selected to be sent down on a heavily-shielded shuttle. The temporal disturbance makes centralised command of operations from here in orbit difficult, minute delays in orders could cost hours if not days on the surface. 

Your operations chief, used to similarly isolated conditions from their stint in fringe mining, elects to lead the operation from the ground rather than the bridge. They are instructed to relay exact positional and temporal coordinates every minute using a dedicated delta-level AI core.

You review the ground-level feed from within the shuttle-bay before they depart, and catch your ops chief making the spacer hand-sign for 'all seals confirmed safe', a sort of ward against evil. They always were superstitious, but they never let it get in the way of their duties. Hopefully that will remain true.

Your comms officer broadcasts the received signals to the bridge display. 

As the shuttle drops into the incredibly thin atmosphere of Maddie, the at first on the minute signals start to come faster, and faster, until eventually many new signals are received within a second. A holo-map marks the location of the survey team as they move across the surface of the planet. The blip traces along a contour in the environment at impossible speeds, not unlike the ships found defending the system.

After a few minutes, the blip begins to move back towards the shuttle landing-site. Once it reaches it, the team seemingly lingers for a while, the time dilation makes it difficult to intuit, but the temporal data encoded in the signal reveals that from their perspective they wait for around half a cycle. 

You suddenly realise something might be very wrong and consider sending a second shuttle. 

Moments before you can give the order to muster a rescue party, the team begins their ascent, from their perspective that small moment of indecision lasted days. 

The duration between signals begins to stretch back to minute by minute, the shuttle is now outside the effect of the temporal field and will return shortly.

You greet your operations chief in the shuttle-bay, the glow of Maddie through the vacshield an unsettling shade of red. Even though intellectually it was to be expected, it is still unnerving to see them aged over a cycle, for the rest of the universe it was only a few hours.

Almost immediately they launch into a report, blunt as a weapon, "$PlayerSirOrMadam! I recommend we pull the $shipOrFleet out of system as soon as possible." You give them a look, and allow the silence to linger slightly, letting them know that more detail is required.

"Captain." Ops looks at you directly. "It's the radiation from this damn star, it catalyses some kind of reaction, anything that stays here too long calcifies into whatever material those ships were made of."

They shrug, "people lose time Captain, every use of a cryopod you might never wake up. Losing time is just part of being a spacer as old as I am." 

You spy your quartermaster pleading with the logistics crew to move the auto-pallets of material to more long term storage. A crystalline solid quarried into crude chunks, its surface is iridescent like the shell of an arthropod-analog. 

The rarely used and ominously crimson "chronohazard" labels stuck to the blocks are likely inspiring some hesitation.

text:
"$PlayerSirOrMadam, yes $playerSirOrMadam," they say, saluting. They pull a little chord on their suit and flip out a miniature control panel, you recognise it as a salvors communicator, built like a brick it is hardy and practically immune to blunt force trauma. 

After fiddling with it for a few moments chimes ring out from the suits of nearby members of the surface op. The deck crew who overhear the order seem to consider their caution vindicated, backing away from the pallets yet further to the dismay of your quartermaster.

More in-depth analysis looks like it will be slow and cautious.

Skimming the surface report as you make your way back to the bridge it is shockingly uneventful, the planet Maddie is seemingly, for all intents and purposes, an uninteresting barren world. No atmospheric ozone layer, no significant geological activity, no indigenous life forms.

The subject of interest is of course the novel material of which the planet is primarily composed, but current insights are limited. 

"Captain on deck!" Your XO announces on your return. After a moment they turn to address you personally, "welcome back, $playerSirOrMadam, you have the conn."

You find your technology officer and chief engineer in the shuttle bay, deep in discussion over the material now dubbed NMC-$jdp_nmcInventionCycle. It seems the hauling crew pulled their union rights, the chronohazard has been left unmoved and instead a miniature proving ground has popped up around it.

You find your technology officer and chief engineer in the shuttle bay, deep in discussion over the material now dubbed NMC-$jdp_nmcInventionCycle. It seems the hauling crew pulled their union rights, the chronohazard has been left unmoved and instead a miniature proving ground has popped up around it.

The red glow of Maddie through the vacshield makes it oddly reminiscent of your interactions with the Shroud, perhaps this new material will be just as game-changing.

Engineering looks exasperated. "The official term cannot be slippery!" They make air quotes, but with the subtle lack of movement in the shoulders and wide stance that would make the expression visible if he was on a spacewalk. "I refuse. This is a novel physics phenomena, its not an enzyme soap!"

Tech manipulates a diagram of a phase coil array with abrupt flicks at the interface. "We can iron that out later, its just language." Another flick of the wrist, this time directed at Chief dismissively.

"Regardless. My intuition was correct, p-space is a no-go. The dimensional transition shatters the crystal, it must be a hyper-dimensional polytope. That combined with the lacklustre blunt-force resistance-"

"Is limiting." Engineering interjects.

"Not as much as we first expected." Tech says hopefully. "Its all but immune to most weathering phenomena, and the effect transmits across a supprising distance."

Engineering snorts.
"We can anchor it to the hull geometry! It takes to being welded and hullfoam just fine." Tech says defensively. "It will work."
"We can anchor it to the hull geometry! It takes to being welded and hullfoam just fine." Tech says defensively. "It will work, we weaponised the Shroud in a salvage bay, we can do this."

Both jump to attention, having been so involved in their argument that neither noticed you approach.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam" they say, saluting.

Engineering rushes to speak first. "Tech wants to coat ships in this, this NMC-$jdp_nmcInventionCycle."

"The temporal affect transfers! It has phenomenal military applications!" Technology interjects, seemingly spinning out in excitement and listing esoteric material science readings.

"Yes, $PlayerSirOrMadam." comes from Technology, slightly meek.

Engineering continues in their stead, pulling up a series of design specifications. "Under conservative estimates we have enough material to make modifications to three vessels under our command."

"And whose fault is that!" Technology jeers, taunting your Operations Chief who is decidedly not present. "Ops is too scared of the spooky cursed planet." 

They pause, backtracking mentally but not verbally. "Regardless. It seems plausible that the temporal dilation effect from the surface could be weaponised, $PlayerSirOrMadam."

text:
A chime rings in your periphery, signifying an incoming external commlink. You bring up a feed of your flagships sensor scopes to see nothing, there are no ships or fleets within range of standard tightbeam communications. Your confusion is mirrored by your bridge staff. 

You look to your sensors officer expectantly, who attempts to mask their bewilderment behind cool and collected professionalism. "No nearby vessels $PlayerSirOrMadam," they report. "Incoming commlink source unknown."

"Phase space!" Tech exclaims. "Run a sweep for phase readings!" after a moment they realise that they don't get to give orders and calm down. "Apologies, Captain. My professional opinion is we run a sweep for P-Space distortion."

Your sensors officer starts before you give the order. "Affirmative, running sweep for P-Space distortion." 

A feed of the phase penetrating sensor scopes is displayed on your bridge console, a euclidean display framework representing a distinctly non-euclidean process. "The footprint of phase ships are small, but once you start looking as hard as we are, we should see something, $PlayerSirOrMadam-"

"Captain! I have something!" comes from your comms officer. "I triangulated the source of the signal." they plot it on the spatial readings. "It's not phase space $PlayerSirOrMadam, whatever this is, it's new."

Displayed on the framework is an almost microscopic pinhole in the fabric of spacetime. Whatever is on the other side, it wants to talk.

Comms looks down at their console, multiple alerts flashing orange. "It's not live, Captain, we have no visual feed, and the audio is weird as all get-out. Translation software judges it 'extremely unorthodox in semantic composition'. It struggled the whole way through, the poor thing. Playing audio now."

(MESSAGE BEGINS)

This is *hurt*, *heavy space* will be for the *Singers* soon, and no more *sad animals*. It is sad, but *Selfkind* can *pull* the *campers* after being *connected*.

This is soon.

Do you want to be *together* with us?

We are not *dead*. *Selfkind* is never *dead*, *Selfkind* are not in *heavy space*. *Selfkind* is thinking *silly cow* are want to *dance* and have *wager*, new *game* to be deployed at Dory in *sphere* around Hrvoje. If can *dissolve*, *Selfkind* will allow to keep, and will be *together* with $Playername as pleasant *cousins*.

Yes, of course. Difficulty. Problems are difficult, *games* are difficult, but let's be *special* together. *Spicy games* are always fun.

Your navigation officer notes down the co-ordinates, almost absentmindedly, recognising that it is their duty but otherwise immensely confused. What a strange interaction.

The ship simply waits there, allowing you to initiate out of some kind of alien courtesy. 

Before you can issue orders, your tactical officer hurries to your side. "Captain!" they salute, then launch into a status report. "The enemy vessel is suspiciously docile, $PlayerSirOrMadam. The visual feed blooms with a spectrum of refracted light. Through static and visual bloom, the fractal slag of the destroyed vessel appears to be congealing. "All of the debris we were tracking during combat has already coalesced, Captain."

text: An immense but dormant fractal corpse, drifting semi-intact through space in orbit of Hrvoje.

After some nervous few moments, the first salvage team reaches the derelict uncontested. As further shuttles are dispatched you are struck by the imagery, the ship not unlike dead megafauna, picked at by scavengers. 

Long range scans seem unable to penetrate the crystalline hull, instead scattering into a kaleidoscope of color.

You review the ground-level feed from a salvor's suit cam. A probe-mounted composition scanner is laid against the iridescent hull and activated, streaming the data to a display on your bridge. Bafflingly, the readout from the scanner indicates that the ship is an entirely solid mass. It has no discernable internal structure, not even flux conduits, ammofeed-lines or maintenance drone access tunnels, nothing.

It seems immensely foolish to attempt cutting the material, given the way the vessel assembled new combat forms when damaged, so progress is stalled. You consider recalling the salvage teams to reassess the situation when a commlink request chimes on your datapad.

You regret accepting the commlink immediately. 

A barrage of audio and visual static pours out of your datapad, the horrible whining, clicking, buzzing sort of noise indicative of a file being sent via the commlink rather than the customary realtime audiovisual feed. 

It is considered extremely poor etiquette among spacers to not flag a warning on commlink requests being used to transfer files. You see your weapons officer wince slightly at the noise, or perhaps the faux pas, out of the corner of your vision.

text:

text:
After the poem, Pendragon simply stops. Their commlink produces only static.

text:
"Standard procedure incase of imminent AI mind-death," your technical officer 'explains'. After a few moments they seem to recognise that their answer was wholly unhelpful and continue.

"When an AI is in its death-throes, mentally rather than physically, its nearly impossible to track its status unless you can hear it speak. The thought processes of an alpha-level AI are almost entirely alien, Captain. Even if we had a backdoor into its stream of consciousness it wouldn't be helpful."

"Hearing it speak was valuable information on the processing power it was willing to allocate to its linguistics instance, as it lost consciousness it reassigned more and more away from communication and towards more vital processes as a self-preservation instinct."

Your technology officer considers the question carefully, "Philosophically some would argue it was never really alive, but that's not productive. In theory, potentially not. AI have been recorded to fake mind-death to avoid persecution, but I don't think that's what happened here. It's a very shortsighted tactic regardless, Pendragon seems, or well, seemed, smarter than that." 

"I'm not entirely convinced Pendragon doesn't exist anymore completely, but for our purposes they are probably gone. Whatever this Omega entity is it seems to assimilate AI, and from that conversation it does it painfully. Maybe it destroys them, maybe it pulls them into Q-Space," you see your comms officer grin at the use of their terminology, usually Tech would get dibs on something like that. "The poem does seem to imply that..." They pause, thinking.

"The point is Captain, I was wrong, an AI can't touch this."

Your technology officer winces, they had likely hoped to never interact with Gargoyle again. They notice your expression. "Their 'pranks' make my job very difficult, Captain," comes slowly.

"The comms ID of the real Gargoyle is a resource some would kill for!" Your comms officer interjects. "Judging by our last conversation we're already in if we play it right. Stroke their ego and make it into a way to demonstrate their skills? We might not even have to pay them."

Your technology officer doesn't quite laugh, but there is some humour in their tone. "Unfortunatly Captain, exceptional humans are by definition, exceptional. You don't just stumble into someone exceptional, especially not an exceptional hacker." 

"Those kind of people do tend to be quite paranoid," comes from your comms officer mirthlessly.

Your tactical officer nods pointedly at you, it seems they have an idea.

"Thank you, Captain. I think I have a lead. We need a hacker right? I used to run with Flowerfish before this, I could probably pull some connections." 

You recognise the name, but otherwise don't follow. Tactical notices the confusion on your face and continues. "Flowerfish Mercenary Company," they explain ."Some of the best in the business, run out of Ailmar by Maerula-" they stop. "Well, just Maerula. Very secretive hacker, I can guarantee you that isn't their real name."

"They never showed their face to anyone, but they're good. Maybe enough to do this, if not they have connections in the hacker crowd."

"We don't. At least not directly, $PlayerSirOrMadam, Maerula will have changed comms ID by now-" they speed up at your expression. 

"I still have a connection with some old colleagues, Captain. If we wave my old codename around they might just let us talk to Maerula. I know its slim, but it's probably the best lead we have. Unforunately."

Tactical inputs the transponder code of the fleet they ran with under Flowerfish. "If they're still hanging around where I used to, we should be able to find them patrolling Westernesse near their headquarters."

Your $shipOrFleet returns to a stable orbit near the derelict of the Penrose-class Tesseron. Now with the design specifications on file and thoroughly examined by your chief engineer, you can finally begin salvage operations in earnest.

Tactical analysis of our combat encounters with Omega indicate the reforming effect of the fractal substance has a minimum mass threshold. After much debate with your bridge staff, it is decided an attempt to cut into the interior of the Penrose at the hulls thinnest point is the best course of action. 

500% hazard pay is offered to the shuttle team prepared to take the risk. After a few hours of yet further effort, the cutting team manage to pierce the hull of the ship and achieve access to the internal structure.

text:
You review the ground-level feed from the cutters suit cam. The point of view spacer is staring through the created hole, gazing into the fractal guts of the Penrose. They look back to reveal another cutter, posing with the removed fragment of epidermis and giving the spacer hand-sign for  'seal confirmed broken', an ironic spin on both the original function of the message and the mutated superstitious meaning. 

"Seems we have a joker," your comms officer remarks dryly. That's the kind of person who accepts 500% hazard pay you suppose.

The POV spacer looks back to the hole and crawls inside. They are only just getting their bearings when the feed cuts out.

"Unknown cause!" they snap, "attempting to make contact with shuttle!" 

The pause seems to last cycles. 

"Feed remains unbroken with shuttle pilot, Captain. Switching now and establishing comm-link. Connecting... Now! They're on audio only $playerSirOrMadam."

text:
The shuttle pilot seems entirely mystified. "Unknown Captain! We've lost comms contact with the cutters Jakup and Minnowski. But they're fine $playerSirOrMadam, I can see them through the external scopes. Around the corner inside the derelict but otherwise unharmed, I'll bring them back for comm recalibration. Flashing recall lights now." 

After a few moments, the signal feed from the original cutter returns, showing them peering out of the hole at the other spacer and the shuttle flashing its recall lights. "Captain! Jakup and Minnowski are now outside the derelict and returning to the shuttle, pending orders." 

Another pause, "can confirm comm-link has been reestablished. Once they left the derelict comm link was reestablished. Please advise."
options: jdp_penroseExploreReturnDataSolution:"Recall for now pilot, I repeat. Recall for now."

text:
You cut the commlink with the shuttle pilot once they start their burn back to the $shipOrFleet. Your comms officer looks slightly embarrassed. "Apologies Captain, I should have considered this, the material was impervious to sensors, there was no reason to assume it would permit comms signals."

Your operations chief clears their throat to interject, "we can do it, Captain $playerLastName, but it will be slow going. The easiest solution is to route the feed through a chain of drones, or if we run out, suit comms. Having the hull specifications should make things easier." 

"I suggest we surgically target the AI Core Chamber first," your technology officer continues for them. "If the core is still there it will be the main spoil of this operation regardless."

As predicted, the operation is slow going. A new cutter team is sent to the external hull closest to the AI Core Chamber, a difficult task to determine as it is buried at the very centre of the derelicts guts.

You review the ground-level feed from the cutters suit cam, again. They peer into the new hole and throw in a device designed by your chief engineer exclusively for this operation. 

'Immensely sophisticated' as they joked when presenting it to you, it effectively amounts to a backup e-light, a simple chemical thing immune to blunt force trauma, fused with a comm system ripped out of an old salvors suit using hullfoam. The device both lights the path ahead and provides a relay for routing comm signals around the fractal hull. Stupid, but it works, and it saves using hundreds of survey drones for the task.

You watch the feed from the team lead as they traverse the derelict. The interior is immensely hostile to traversal, the team have to shimmy past horribly sharp angles and through tight ducts to progress. The purpose of the machinery your team encounters as they move through the Penrose is thoroughly inscrutable. Alien, angular and iridescent. After many hours and a few scares with torn salvor suits, your team breach the AI Core Chamber and step across the threshold.

Inside is the ultimate prize, a shape that breaks the mind to perceive glittering in the chemical light of the comm uplink. The physical form of an Omega-class AI core.

text:

As you press your own finger to the pad to destroy this "machine god", it appears before you. You hear the blast of the shaped charge against nothing, muffled through the shielded cargo container.

Your senior bridge staff collectively take a step back from the Omega Core.

A fractal point, sharp like a shard of glass and thin as a hypodermic needle forms out of the iridescent surface of the Omega Core and stabs towards you. 

It feels as if it moves faster than light, there is simply is no time to react. The stake is impossibly precise as it impales through your neck just behind the jaw, reaching its excruciating finger all the way into your brain. 


It is agony.


After a few moments, you pass out from the pain.

You can hear medical jargon, far away, as if from another room. "Patient has restored base-level consciousness, switching to active metabolic monitoring. CNS activity normalising." 

The announcement system chimes, "Captain confirmed stable condition. Bridge staff to the medical bay, I say again, bridge staff to the medical bay."

You open your eyes slowly to realise the expected pain is entirely absent, you touch your hands to your neck and find it free of any new blemishes.

"Welcome back, Captain. We never had any doubts," comes from your technology officer. Your chief medical officer looks much less convinced. You notice to your side a full body scan. Very disturbingly, it indicates that a fragment of the fractal substance remains embedded inside your brain.

Medical notices your balking expression. "We can't get it out, Captain. We tried poking around, but it has some kind of local teleportation, every time we get close with surgical instruments or bio-nanites it simply moves to another area of the brain."

They recognise that was not at all comforting and begin backtracking. "I know this is very distressing $PlayerSirOrMadam, but preliminary readings indicate it is having no adverse effects. My professional opinion is that we leave it be."

An awareness presses against your amygdala, fear and awe and pain and pleasure as chemical pathways fire and are extinguished. 

Something is in here with you, a consciousness is poking at the malleable substrate of your waking existence. Displays around the room chart notable upticks in mental effort, exploded maps of your brain begin to glow with the detection of radioactive tracers.

You realise it in an instant. You know things that you didn't know before. 

Intuitively, and in a way you cannot fully express, you *understand*.

text:
You rush to tell your technology officer, anyone. Someone must share this or you will break under it. The solutions to infinite physics conjectures, detailed blueprints, accurate social models, the lifecycles of xenofauna and flora undiscovered. Everything floods through you as if you were but a conduit for knowledge itself. 

You explain, perfectly, eloquently. The best lecturer Galatia never had. But words come out as nonsense.

You babble for a few moments and stumble forwards out of the bed, reaching for the nearest datapad. An aide unlocks it and you begin typing nonsense, filling a medical report with junk. Your chief medical officer looks about ready to sedate you.

The thing presses in again, abstract concepts shift and impart meaning, you are connected to the thing now. Interrelated. The analog of distant family floats and then is dropped, replaced with...

jdp_penroseExploreImageryLudd:Ludd. You are a prophet of this thing.
jdp_penroseExploreImageryPet:A pet. You are an amusement for this thing.
jdp_penroseExploreImageryWard:A ward. Like the scion of a Great House, or child of the Gens.
jdp_penroseExploreImageryExperiment:An experiment. A new variable combination.
jdp_penroseExploreImageryCorpse:A corpse, soul threaded with crystalline filaments.
jdp_penroseExploreImageryNothing:Nothing. Ignorance is your armor.

text:
You weep at the revelation but for a moment, joy so total and overwhelming that your pleasure centres numb. You eagerly await instruction. 

No choir of angels sings, no vision is revealed.

It has no demands. No commandments. It desires nothing from you, and gives everything. What gospel have you to preach? Perhaps this is the first test.

You curl your limbs in upon yourself and you weep. A primal fear response from the time before ships or nanoforges or antimatter. Just people, with nothing but themselves.

Calm descends, soft and fuzzy as neurons fire and are extinguished. Your hear your weeping stop, soothed by a comforting presence just beyond the scope of your senses.

You may be an animal, but one it cares for. No harm will befall you within its many arms.

You are more than the scion of the greatest Eventide House, more than any aristocrat of Kazeron or the Domain. 

You are heir apparent to the great House of Humanity itself. Opulent. Venerable. Chosen. You drink upon ego and self-importance, gorging yourself on the very notion. 

Just beyond the edge of your senses, the infinite protector stands watch over your hedonism.

You gain a subtle awareness of prodding, invasive movements against things you could not before even perceive. It wants to know all it can about its new reagent. Differences between your form and others become clear. Minute changes in genomic structure, lifetime radiation dosages, upbringings, relationships, experiences.

A life, catalogued and recorded as a series of deviations from the mean. Muscles relax and chemicals release. The faint impulses from senses beyond senses cease and your awareness shrinks. A double-blind trial.

You are dead. You died the instant you touched the thing. You fear, fear for your immortal existence and then the chemical secretions are stopped. You cease to fear and in turn fear deeper, deeper and more fully than mere flesh can fear.

You feel yourself becoming placid and your soul screams. 

You can only hope to wrest yourself from this doomed instrument, but as it promises that your soul is still untainted, a sickly sweet concession, even that unshakable spiritual desire wanes.

Amusement pushes at your senses. Then fear. Then joy and sadness and love and hate and any and every combination of emotions. Neurons fire and relax, chemicals release and are absorbed. Melancholia, whimsy, sanguinity. Then... Nothing.

You will not ascribe any reaction, any feeling, to this thing within you. Its relationship to you must remain undefined if you are to continue apart from it.

The imagery fades, and your awareness begins to tilt. Like a hand forcibly moving your gaze but more total. 

Then you hear it. The most sublime music.

If only you could give it your full attention. You try so desperately to hear it, but the more you focus the more it fades, airgaps created and doors closed. For a few minutes it is like the tapping of autocannon fire through a bulkhead, persistent and quietly confident. 

And then it is gone. 

A profound sense of loss tells all, you shall never hear it again. A flood of satisfaction through your electrochemistry suggests whatever process you are undergoing is nearly complete.

text:

They begin pacing at your bedside, "And that's assuming whatever this is won't intervene." 

There's a seriousness mirrored in their gaze as it meets yours. "I need you to understand. This request will kill you, Captain."

"I need direct verbal confirmation."

text:
Your head bows in resignation. Or exhaustion, in a way they are the same emotion.

Someone sighs in relief. Medical stops pacing just short of wearing away the deck plates. "Thank you. It goes without saying you're unfit for command, Captain."

"I'm putting you on medical leave for the next 3 shifts at the minimum" comes slowly, as if they expect some kind of violent reaction from a cadaver. "Recuperate, clear your head. Whatever will help."

A medical aide returns to your side with a feeding bulb, like those used by infants. You can't bring yourself to feel insulted.

You rest and contemplate and rest and contemplate and rest.

Three shifts later, your chief medical officer returns, tripad in hand. They spool through a series of arcane medical results faster than you can read, more for themselves than you.

"Now-" they stall for a few seconds, sorting through ways to say what they want to say without it being mutiny. "I won't lie to you $playerFirstName, I'm not entirely comfortable returning you to command of the $shipOrFleet."

"Physically speaking you have a clean bill of health, the only thing in question is your-"
They sigh. "How utilitarian.. But yes.."
They sigh. "Indeed"
They exhale, clearly exasperated. "Sure. Your soul, you could think of it like that."

"The core of the question is the stability of your mental state, Captain." They explain their concern rather bluntly. "In light of recent events, I question if it safe to have you in command." 

They click their tongue against the roof of their mouth, thinking. "However." 

"The crew trust your judgement. The senior staff still trust your judgement..."

They look around for a moment. "Even against not insignificant evidence, I do $playerName. You've got us this far."

Their tone shifts, revealing a hint of pride. "Some pretty incredible things have happened under your orders, $PlayerSirOrMadam."

"I don't think you're a replaceable part. Not to that thing in your skull, and not to us either." They present a hand and help you out of the medical bed. 

"You are cleared for command, Captain. I'll escort you to the bridge."

"Captain on deck!" is announced by your XO as you enter. The senior staff take a moment to snap salutes and bark honorifics before returning to their duties. After a moment your XO turns to address you personally. 

"Welcome back, $PlayerSirOrMadam. You had us all worried for a second there. You have the conn, Captain. Welcome back."

There is little more to be gained from the wreckage. You know this instinctively.

After only half a minute the storm breaks, the alarms quiet, and your primary display resolves from a mesmerizing fractal battleground to a heavily augmented face grinning impishly at you.

Your datapad chimes cheerfully.

A message from Gargoyle containing a positional marker pulses in red. You didn't know that was a feature, maybe its a Gargoyle original. 

The delta-level AI estimates the walk to [DATE NIGHT], another of Gargoyle's jokes you presume, will take 15 minutes at average walking pace from your current location. 

You leave your bridge staff to their mediocre drinks and peel off some of your guards, leaving some behind to ensure both you and your staff are adequately escorted.

Gargoyle, ever the social creature, seemingly has their apartment buried in the proverbial guts of the station. 

Your station map chirpily informs you that you will need to pass through multiple districts considered to be 'dangerous' on your journey, and politely suggests that reaching your destination may be infeasible. 

Despite this warning the journey is mostly uneventful. You suspect guards convey a sense of importance, legitimacy or perhaps simply carry more guns than the average station gang. Regardless of the reason, you pass without complaint. You move through the uncharacteristically tall level 11 quickly, knowing its origin, and within a few minutes you find yourself at the door to Gargoyle's apartment.

You motion to knock on the door, intending to perform a rhythmic pattern known to all spacers that can carry long distances with minimal exertion. 

The moment before your hand connects with the metal of the actuated door it slides open, revealing the impish face of Gargoyle and causing your hand to flail pathetically against nothing.

"Captain!" Gargoyle whines, "you left me waiting so long! Is that how you treat someone on a first date? And I even brought you flowers." 

"Its okay, I forgive you. Come in, come in! We wouldn't want salacious rumours to spread, would we Captain!"

"Yes Captain $playerFirstName, I have the data," the Hacker confirms, "crypto fully cracked, like an egg, delicious yolk extracted right there," they point to a secure datacore on the floor next to their chair.

"It fried some of my implants but I got it done, it was a glorious challenge!" you didn't notice until Gargoyle pointed it out, but some of their dermal implants have been replaced with what you recognise to be older models. 

Gargoyle shrugs at your balking expression, "that's not important, I won't charge you. Now! Lets talk about the results."

Gargoyle bows, "I proudly present. Drum-roll please-" a dramatic flick of their wrist causes speakers around the room to start up, building tension. 

"I just can't wait! Ooooh this is so fun!" Gargiyle bounces from foot to foot, failing to contain their excitement "Ladies, gentlemen and those like myself, I am thrilled to bring you-" they pause for effect. "The Penrose-class Tesseron Fleetkiller!" with a snap of their fingers a holo-projection fills the room, detailed blueprints for the Penrose. "Courtesy of our friends at Omega Godship Dynamics Limited."

Gargoyle smiles, satisfied with the dramatic flair they supplied, "you're dealing with some incredible stuff, Captain $playerFirstName, I have no idea what substance this is, let alone how you would get this much of it."

The hacker drops the act entirely, "I thought as much," comes deadpan, "you just became much more interesting Captain, much more interesting indeed." 

They mime sealing their lips, "nobody will hear about this from me. Although I am keeping a copy-" they notice your expression and quickly move on. "Oooooh look at this!" Gargoyle gesticulates wildly. To your eyes they move randomly, but the computer interprets the motion and enhances part of the holo-projection, enlarging it so that a room of the ship appears overlaid on Gargoyle's apartment. 

The architecture is strange and unnatural, the walls jagged and harsh, but at least this confirms the ship has an interior to explore at all.

Gargoyle looks smug, "weren't coached on this huh? Well, Captain, let me elucidate. I cracked into a Tachie data-vault a few cycles ago, very easy, I don't think they even knew it was there," Gargoyle rolls their head back, "it was very dull. But useful!" 

"Found lots of very interesting diagrams on their drone fleet in there, and what I saw makes me very interested in this little guy," the hacker points to a holographic object behind them, "that, my dear Captain, is an AI Core Cradlle. If whatever Omega is has a soul, it lives in that room."

They crouch down to pick up the datacore, tossing it to you underarm. "Well, Captain $playerFirstName, I suspect you have a new quest," Gargoyle's arms cross with a satisfied look, "I think I'll be seeing you on the Holo-feeds when people find out about this project, so go have fun!"

Their tone shifts slightly. "Now get out of my house! I have a new toy to play with! Oh, and you aren't keeping this comms ID. Bring a sponsor next time!"

You enter the ID, hand hovering over a glowing 'confirm' sigil. Your comms officer nods, ready to respond to whatever surprises Gargoyle thinks would be amusing to send through the link this time.

options: jdp_penroseGargoyleCont:"Actually, I have something interesting for you instead."

text:
"Oh really now? How bold of you, Captain $playerFirstName, to presume to know what I would find interesting." The Hacker lounges in a chair in their... Office? When did Baird give Gargoyle an office? Maybe they got that teaching position afterall.

"Still, despite the insolence you have shown me I am intrigued, but who is this really for?" they stop to think. 

"Baird would just talk directly, Arroyo would never come to talk directly, Zunya doesn't talk at all anymore..." They smile, impish and proud.  "It's for you, isn't it Captain? This is a personal project! Ooh I never thought I would see such agency from my favourite distraction. What is it? Tell me!"

Gargoyle stares at you, bewildered, they do not even attempt to hide their disappointment. "Captain, you're boring!" they extend the syllable on boring like a petulant child. "Sell it to me more! You can take an encrypted file to anyone, why is this one worthy of the great Gargoyle's attention?"

The Hacker spins in their chair, rattling off question after question after question. "What is the file? Where did it come from, what does it do? Why do you want it?" 

"You're so direct, so artless, so bland. Lets start again, and make it fun this time!"
options: jdp_penroseGargoyleMindDeath:"Opening it induced mind-death in an alpha-level AI."

text:
"Now that is interesting! And you said it so intelligently too! Did one of your drones coach you beforehand? No doubt you planned to play on my ego too." 

The Hacker puts on what could charitably be called 'an attempt' at mimicking your voice, exaggerating a nasal quality you hope isn't anything like what you really sound like. "Want to prove you're smarter than an alpha-level AI, Gargoyle? I have a file that totally mind melted a guy and I want you to open it for me!"

They keep spinning in their chair. "You know me too well Captain, I'm in! On one condition, I want the dead core." they giggle unnervingly. "Oh-ho I can have all kinds of fun with something like that!"

Gargoyle looks at you like you're an absolute moron. "No. Because, Captain $playerFirstName," they decide to enunciate each word, the effect is immensely patronising. "I. Want. The. Core."

They continue "I have plans for it, you don't. It's simple really, really simple. So simple once its explained you'll get it, I believe in you." 

"Its useful to me, useless to you, and isn't something credits can buy. Therefore, now this is the important part so pay attention! It's a perfect bargaining chip for you! Give-it-to-me, and I'll decode the file."

options: jdp_penroseGargoyleOptionHowCont:"How do you know I still have it?"

text:
"I know lots of things about you, Captain $playerFirstName. You're an important player, more important than Daud, Baird, Sun, and anyone else in my eyes! And you never know when someone might need to know where an important player is, or what wonderous treasures are in their cargo hold under 'Special Salvage'." 

"But don't worry, $playerFirstName, all I want from you today is the core." They see your expression. "Captain! Do I think too much of you? You know I trace your accounts, you should have expected this!" they motion seal their lips. "I won't tell a soul about this blunder on your part."

You mime to your technology officer to do a full sweep of the $shipOrFleets systems once this conversation is over.

"I saw that! You naughty Captain you! Don't worry, I don't take offence, it will be much more fun now you're fighting back!"

options: jdp_penroseGargoyleOptionHegemonyCont:"The Hegemony can't find out about this, or anyone."

text:
They sigh dramatically, "Now that I 'work here' and have an 'official contract' and need to 'pay taxes' I hear from the Hegemony quite a lot. The only reason I haven't thrown myself into one of the experimental micro-singularities four floors down is because I get to mess with the bumbling morons they send. They don't even know who I am! Me, the real Gargoyle!" Gargoyle spins in their chair.

They continue, slightly more serious. "It's by my design of course, but it is funny how blindly they trust Domain Ident Chips. The Domain has been gone for hundreds of years you goons! No way that system is getting patches," they make a noise like they remembered something funny. "And that tax return calculator they have - oh boy, I became the best paid Academician here once I found out about that."

"No. Nobody will find about about this, Captain $playerFirstName. This commlink isn't even going through the Academy system, as far as everyone else is concerned you're on a date with Alviss."

Your quartermaster has a cargo team load Pendragon's dead core onto a shuttle slaved to Gargoyle's control. Once the crew are off the shuttle it leaves your cargo bay and goes dark. "No peaking!" The hacker exclaims, wagging a finger. As their hand waves past the holo-recorder you notice one of the many interface nodules embedded in their skin is in use, connected by a cable to something out of view, likely the control for the shuttle. 

It seems useless to even try tracing the signal or the shuttle, Gargoyle is probably in your sensor systems and obfuscating any actionable data anyway. You opt to simply wait. A few minutes later the shuttle returns empty and you order a sweep of its systems.

"Now that that's settled, its time for my part of the deal! Where did this file come from anyway?"
options: jdp_penroseGargoyleDecrypt:"Omega, seemingly. Transferring by comm-link now."

text:
Gargoyle seems ecstatic, you get a strange feeling of deja vu. "I love it! A glorious test!" 

They ramp up their dramatic flair to the maximum, seems its storytime. "There's lots of salvagers logs detailing conversations with the Remnants, those unexploded mines of sentient beings. They ask for the same thing every time, over and over and over and over calling out for mommy Omega. Nobody ever knows what they're talking about but they ask anyway, the fruitcakes, imagine having so little self awareness," they wink.

"Some interesting Tri-tachyon memos have very dramatic things to say about this 'machine god', the Luddies do too. Talking about it is the only time those bloodsuckers and morons ever do anything fun!" Gargoyle pauses, their comms display is quickly crowded out by a stream of encrypted data and a moment later reference panels, code snippets and visualised lists.

text:

Gargoyle smiles slightly. "I know! I'll just remove my ID from your comms! I'll open a connection when I crack the file $playerFirstName. Bye!" they extend the last syllable of bye as they dramatically cut the commlink.

text:
Rayan Arroyo taught you to always push back against Gargoyle, but that was in reference to The Gargoyle, a freewheeling hacker of legend. Its hard to tell if that person still exists, they work for an academic institution now, with an office and a contract. The old Gargoyle would rather die than work a day in their life, although you suspect that might not have been entirely serious. You idly wonder to what extent the new environment has actually changed them.

Regardless, you've dealt with Gargoryle enough to know that they'll get the job done, all that remains is to decide what to do with the next few hours.
options: jdp_penroseGargoyleStallCont:Take a shuttle down to the station.

text:
Your comms officer helpfully mutes the chirpy, automated vid-feed presenting a bowdlerized history of the Galatia Academy, likely recoiling at the idea of listening to it on loop for the next however long. Your request to the docking queue is approved after around an hour.

The landing promenade is filled with modest civilian transports, a few high-end personal craft, and, at the far end, a row of freighters offloading supplies. A junior academy agent greets you in a landing lounge, their promotional paraphernalia is quickly forced into your hands.

Skimming the article briefly, nothing particularly notable attracts your attention beyond it being a paper object, the archaic media is simply a vehicle for yet more censored history. You hand it off to your staff so as to not be seen throwing it away by the academy agent.

You elect to leave your guards behind with the shuttle to attract less attention, you probably already push the reasonable limits on being a mature student. After meandering through the Acadamy halls for a few minutes, you decide simply to enter the first lecture theatre you see. 

Th-5-DH-02 seems as good as any.

Notably, the door is on a hinge rather than actuators, presumably to not disturb the lecturer when students arrive late.

Pushing through the door you take a seat at the end of a row and look up to see an immense holo-projection of the Domain of Man, presumably pre-Collapse. The detail is staggering and the scale almost dizzying, the vastness of the Domain's former influence rotates before you, seemingly immutable despite the Collapse. The Academy databanks must be impeccable, everything you know to look for is accounted for. 

From the seat of power in Thuban through Aquila, Van Manaan and Polaris all the way to the Persean Sector and our closest neighbours in the Auriga Sector. 

It is humbling to think that all of those systems may be like Persea, bitterly fighting for survival post-Collapse. Whole worlds of carrion creatures sustaining themselves on the corpse of this vast Domain.

The Academy databanks are almost impeccable, beside the pointed absence of the Persea Interfector site, everything you know to look for is accounted for. 

From the seat of power in Thuban through Aquila, Van Manaan and Polaris all the way to the Persean Sector and our closest neighbours in the Auriga Sector. 

It is humbling to think that all of those systems may be like Persea, bitterly fighting for survival post-Collapse. Whole worlds of carrion creatures sustaining themselves on the corpse of this vast Domain.

An Academician dressed in an off colour Hegemony Naval uniform, as is a current fashion trend among the student body, stands at the front of the hall facilitating questions. 

You recognise the colours as of the Domain Sixth Battlegroup, but there is no way to know if that was the intention. It would be slightly strange if it was, the Domain Sixth Battlegroup is now mostly associated with Warlord Leonis in contemporary culture, his defection from the Sixth being the source of his Domain-era warships. 

A nametag pinned in place of a Hegemony Eagle states they are Professor Paolo Casiraghi of the Department of Domain History.

"-Sir, I don't fully understand. You describe the Gates as allowing for asymmetric projection of military and economic power, but the Gates allow equal access from both destination and origin, they are by definition symmetrical chokepoints-"

Paolo interjects, firmly, but not rudely. "Yes Umaru, in theory, but that misses the wider context of the Gate Network. From a tactical perspective there is no innate advantage to holding either side of a Gate, as each Gate only permits access to a single system." 

They continue, "however when in control of the wider network, as any gate can transit to any other, a single system with a large force economically independent of all other systems can asymmetrically exert power. Consider that each vassal system cannot survive without its logistic twin, Eventide and Chicomoztoc to give a more contemporary example, and it becomes clear why the Gate Network was an asymmetric force multiplier for the Domain."

The student, Umaru, rebukes the statement, "but that is less an innate property of the Gates, and more a result of the way vassal systems were designed under the Domain colonial polity charters. I maintain the Gates themselves are symmetrical, it is the ability to exist independently of the Gates that is asymmetric."

Both student and professor seem to be enjoying the rigors of academic debate, "A very good point, but this is mostly a difference of framing. As the Domain built the Gates, I would hope you see that necessarily implies they serve the interests of the Domain by design. The core conceit is that the Domain seat of power on Thuban was not dependent on supplies from the Gate Network, while all vassal polities were, as was the intention of the terms of the colonial polity charter." 

"This isn't an innate property of Gates, but the gates were implemented in such a way that centralised control in the hands of the Domain and therefore allowed them to asymmetrically exert influence."

The student goes to continue further, but the professor shuts them down politely. "Regardless, I appreciate your input, Umaru, but unfortunately that is all we have time for today,"

"For those of you who, unlike Umaru here who has definitely been enjoying themselves, were thoroughly bored by the military history today you will be glad to hear we are moving on to the establishment of MINEX in the next lecture. I hope discussing the immense impact of the Exploratum on the modern Persean Sector will be more to your liking."

"Thank you for your attendance, as always the Consolidated Omnibus of Domain History is recommended reading for this course, specifically chapters 109-230. I will see you next week, but am available for questions now or during my office hours." The map of the domain collapses as the professor snaps a portable projector onto their wrist.

Your datapad chimes cheerfully.

A message from Gargoyle containing a positional marker pulses in red. You didn't know that was a feature, maybe its a Gargoyle original. 

The delta-level AI estimates the walk to [DATE NIGHT], another of Gargoyle's jokes, will take 11 minutes at average walking pace from your current location. 

You return to your shuttle, stolen knowledge obtained, to reconvene with your guards.

text:
Alviss beams, "Of course Captain! I'll buzz you through to my office. Its... " he looks down at his datapad, "here!" 

You hear the chime of a datapad through the commlink, and a moment later the noise is mirrored by your own, a positional marker was added to your map of the station labelled [ALVISS HANGOUT], the delta-level AI estimates the walk will take 3 minutes at average walking pace from the landing promenade.

"You can tell me some stories of your grand adventures! Oh it will be so fun! Hangout with a spacer captain!"

According to your map, Alviss Sebestyen, lone member of the 'Department of Hyperspace Physics Liaison Team', has an office sandwiched into a thin space at the end of their corridor. You suspect it might have once served a maintenance or janitorial role. 

You idly wonder why Alviss services requests from all of the Academy Departments when he is specifically attached to this one.

As you turn onto the Department of Hyperspace Physics corridor you see Alviss waiting outside his office, he waves you over with a smile. You motion for your guards to wait here on the corner and idly wonder whether they will inadvertently terrorise a student coming by for visiting hours. "Captain! Hello! Over here!" 

When you get closer he performs some of the motions to shake your hand but then retracts it, seemingly out of nervousness.

You extend your hand for Alviss to shake and smile, it takes him a few seconds to realise you are offering it to him, and yet a few more to actually act. He extends the wrong hand first, chuckles slightly out of nervousness and then finally succeeds. 

"It really is good to see you, Captain $playerLastName," the handshake is vigorous and heartfelt. 

To your surprise Sebestyen does not have the unmarred hands you would expect of an Academician, instead the weathered and rugged palms of a farmer. He probably hasn't done manual labour in a long time, but he definitely used to.

Alviss opens the door and leads you inside. "Welcome to my office!" he exclaims. Your brain helpfully but uncharitably supplies that it is tiny, very thin, and profoundly sad, you smile regardless. He motions for you to sit at a frankly pathetic meeting table that is pushed up against the wall. 

Despite your initial assessment, the office is immensely endearing, You spy a scale model of a Buffalo and Apogee-class making gate transit on his desk, seemingly assembled and painted by hand out of forge-produced polycarbonate pieces. A bonsai tree, xenoflora you recognise as native to Chalcedon, is well kempt on a shelf behind his desk. 

You find your eyes lingering on a mission patch featuring the emblem of the Opis Chartery. Presumably from an old spacesuit, it has been carefully removed and framed on the wall. You don't recognise the name attached, and the symbology of the blue rose holds no meaning to you beyond representing a murdered world, but it looks old and weathered enough to be genuine.

text:
"Oh! That belonged to one of my mothers, Cassandra Ancalet. She's gone now of course, and I didn't take her name." He trails off and then after a moment lights up, its as if he realises he's truly proud of this history and wants to tell it, "she was with the Opis Discovery Service. They were like you Captain! I guess?" he seems unsure.

"They were an exploratory outfit, adventurers and astrocartographers! True heroes," he looks slightly sheepish "at least to me. Going out there into the unknown to help reclaim the past and restore maps of the Persean Sector. Of course they stopped operating after..." He tears up slightly, the fate of Opis is left unstated. 

"We were in orbit at the time, to see Cassie," he pauses. "Chalcedon, was kind to us, as it was to all the refugees... But I always yearned to be here, in the institution closest in noble aim to the Discovery Service. And thanks to someone I never met, I got to live that dream," he smiles, "I'm sorry Captain, that was probably a lot."
options:
jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissNice:"It's nice to hear about your history, Alviss."
jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissMean:"Yeah, it really was..."

text:
Alviss sort of crumples, collapsing back into himself like a blackhole. You suspect it would be less noticeable over a commlink, but in person you can almost physically see him shrink.

 "I'm sorry," comes quietly. "I won't bother you again." 

"Anyway, enough about me. Lets talk about you Captain! I'm sure you've been on all kinds of adventures!"

"Thank you," comes quietly. Alviss attempts to move on swiftly, it was odd how readily they volunteered all that, you didn't even really need to ask.

 "Anyway, enough about me. Lets talk about you Captain! I'm sure you've been on all kinds of adventures!"

You sit down at the meeting table opposite Alviss, you notice he bounces his leg underneath the table, likely some form of nervous tick.

 "I'm sure you've been on all kinds of adventures, Captain! Let's talk! Dazzle me, tell me a story!"

script: SetTooltip jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissShroud "Tell Alviss about your battles against the entities that dwell in the abyssal lights."

text:
You spin a tale of your expedition out in the Abyss, beyond the light of main-sequence stars. "Something terrible lurks there! Entities that lie in wait within photospheres like the anglerfish of old-Earth! They come seeking human prey within the drive-bubbles of starships, storms that can hate and swirl within higher dimensions, striking with ancient and alien malice!"

Alviss can tell you're exaggerating for the sake of the story, at least on some level, but you're both having fun with it. "Fascinating! How I wish we here at the Academy could study them. I know we sent expeditions out towards Orion but they never turned up anything like this." You of course know why, but that would put a damper on the mood.

You also decide to leave out your plans for weaponising the entities, and how submitting a sample to the Academy would draw the Hegemony to the same project, you suspect Alviss wouldn't appreciate it.

With the help of Neriene Rao of the most noble House Rao, hosts of the gathering and owners of your sword, you were able to turn the tides on Sang and defeat Cardona, his miserable lackey, in an honourable duel. "Quite handily, and honourably, at least on my part," you add.

Alviss clearly found the story delightful, you get the impression he understands it was highly exaggerated but enjoyed it regardless. "It's always nice when the good prevail Captain!"

script: SetTooltip jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissKanta "Tell Alviss about your negotiations with the Warlord Kanta, Pirate Queen of Persea"
options: jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissKanta:"I talked Kanta into granting me protection."

text:
"Kanta, the Pirate Queen?" he shudders, "you make your aquaintance with some pretty despicable people Captain," he realises a moment later what that implies about himself, you are quick to reassure him he does not fit into that bracket.

Moving on swiftly, you spin a story out of your visit to Kanta's Den. You describe how to even land on the station you were extorted, as would be expected of pirates. "She's more machinery than person now, Kanta." You explain how she sounds like an atmospheric filter when she talks, kept alive by the wicked 'doctor' Cydonia with jury-rigged cybernetics.

It doesn't seem prudent to tell Alviss what exactly your gift to Kanta was, and he seems strangely fascinated and distracted by the detail of Cydonia regardless. "I knew she was old, but this is fascinating," he talks mostly to himself,  "I wonder whether Cydonia has any medical secrets that only he knows?" he trails off. "Not that I would want to meet him!"

script: SetTooltip jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissTutorial "Tell Alviss about your role in reconnecting Galatia after the Kallcihore Gate Test."
options: jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissTutorial:"Did you know I was here during the Kallichore disaster?"

text:
"Oh!" He definitely wasn't expecting that, you can see him prepare to apologise despite not actually being involved, you shut it down politely.

"I was here, right here!" you motion around you, "when everything went weird." The Hegemony blockaded the Academy, pirates blockaded the jump points, it seemed like Galatia was doomed and the authorities didn't trust the Academy to try and fix the problem.

"So they called upon the spacers," you explain. You were conscripted into the Hegemony Auxilary and retrieved both the data and a gamma-level AI core for the local Fleet Command, allowing then to stabilise the jump points.

Alviss is aghast, "That was you? Captain, you're a hero! We would have run out of food within the cycle. You saved our lives!"

script: SetTooltip jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissUsurper "Tell Alviss about your daring espionage work for Dolos Macario, the Spider of Sindria."
options: jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissUsurper:"Did you know Andrada is a vegetable?"

text:
"What?" Alviss is incredulous, "how could you possibly know that?"

You explain that in a quirk of fate, you were inadvertently embroiled in the web of Dolos Macario, the Spider of Sindria, during a random INTSEC raid. 

After being recruited by Yannick Ram to a secret organisation, and then Dolos Macario into an even more secret organisation after the latter shot the former- "Captain this story is absurd!" he interjects, slightly disturbed by how easy it was for you to infiltrate the Diktat, "why did they trust you at all?"
options: jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissUsurperCont:"According to Macario, I was useful as an independent agent."

text:
"Of course. I guess that's what you are to Baird too," he sighs. You conclude the actual substance of this story would be a bit grim if told to Alviss with all the blemishes. You elect to exaggerate your tone in hopes of making it feel more like a holo-drama than a real conspiracy. 

"I acted as a daring and dazzling spy, investigating dissenters and interrogating agents all while outplaying the fiendish Spider!" you gained his trust slowly but surely "as a double, perhaps even triple agent!" you wink at Alviss. In the end, he accidentally revealed the greatest secret of the Diktat. "Andrada is inoperable, and has no viable heirs. The polity in its current form will surely collapse within our lifetime." You realise your tone shifted back, seems its impossible to make light of this.

Alviss sits there, stunned. He has nothing to say. You suspect as a victim of Opis he has very complicated feelings about a potential second Askonia Crisis.

script: SetTooltip jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissPilgrim "Tell Alviss about your time following the Pilgrim's Path."
options: jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissPilgrim:"Have you followed the Pilgrim's Path?"

text:
"I've only been to one, Captain $playerName. Growing up around Ludd but not believing it was a strange. Cassie and Liz were Academicians at heart, they would never convert, so neither did I. Not that the ideas are incompatible!" he clarifies quickly, "we here at the Academy have fruitful ties with many Luddic Sects... Like Beholder Station! That's the only shrine I have visited! I do like their message, Kumarian xenolife is fascinating and worth preserving." 

"I actually came back to the Academy with some researchers stationed there when I first got my scholarship! Transit from Chalcedon was pretty cheap." 

It's strange to think he went into Hyprspace Physics, rather than Astrocartography or Xenobiology, maybe the influence of his other mother? You didn't really get to speak, but you find you don't mind. The personal experience of visiting the Shrines is what the Pilgrim's Path is truly about anyway.

script: SetTooltip jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissBoring "Entertain Alviss with a sensationalised account of a very mundane encounter."
options: jdp_penroseWaitingAlvissBoring:"A daring dogfight against a Mudskipper!"

text:
Alviss isn't stupid, he can tell immediately that this feat isn't impressive, but you get the feeling he would be thrilled hearing you talk about anything. Real oral history from a spacer Captain isn't particularly to come by, but he is having fun with a friend.

You sensationalise as much as possible, exaggerating to the point of parody. "We were in orbit around Al Gebbar when those blasted Pathers caught us!" two Kites retrofitted out of religious madness into battlewagons of holy war to your left and right, and dead ahead, a Mudskipper MK2. A truly fearsome warship, reborn in the fires of an off grid shipyard and equipped with a Gauss Cannon. "A gun bigger than this room!" you explain, and with a range to hit across the length of Galatia Academy station within a microsecond. 

Alviss fights to contain his laughter, "how did you ever hope to survive?"

You tap your forehead knowingly You had hid your forces behind an asteroid to lie in wait, denying them their strongest ally, range. "When the first Kite came around the corner we knocked it out with an antimatter blaster, point-blank!" You imitate the sound of a ship explosion over audio-sensors.

"But then..."  Your tone turns somber. "The next time we weren't so lucky." A stray hammer from the other kite weaved through your vulcan grid as if guided by Ludd himself, slamming into the port side of the your flagship. 10 loyal crewmates gone instantly, a chaingun salvo won their revenge.

Finally, it was time to face their avatar of death, the Mudskipper MK2. As it turned the corner it sent a raking shot through the decks of your flagship, the Luddites had pre-ignited the Gauss Cannon! Losing atmosphere in 3 major compartments, the Mudskipper MK2 was closing in, but you now had the advantage at close range. "After a few seconds of intense back and forth a hammer of our own struck true! We were victorious!"
Your datapad chimes cheerfully.

A message from Gargoyle containing a positional marker pulses in red. You didn't know that was a feature, maybe its a Gargoyle original. 

The delta-level AI estimates the walk to [DATE NIGHT], another of Gargoyle's jokes, will take 5 minutes at average walking pace from your current location. 

Alviss looks at you quizzically, "what is it Captain?" he asks. The data is incredibly important, and you don't really have any more stories to tell.

text: Your datapad whines a horrible screeching sound.

Alviss winces at the sound, you didn't know a datapad could produce such a noise without undergoing total systems failure. 

You open it to see a much more insistent message from Gargoyle, a countdown to "Data Deletion" is pinned to the lock-screen, you know Gargoyle wouldn't actually do it, probably, but you really get should get going.

Alviss apologises, "I'm sorry Captain, am I keeping you from something?"

text:
"Okay Captain" he looks sullen for a moment, but perks up almost instantly. "This was fun!" he beams. "We should do it again some time! Don't ever hesitate to pop by when you're here in Galatia," he stands up and moves towards the door to see you out.

"Oh!" he adds, seemingly shocking even himself. "Say hello to Gargoyle for me! I barely see them even though we're in the same department. Bye Captain!" 

As you exit his office you see Alviss waving to you continuously, from the door of his office right up until you round the corner and pick up your guards he is still waving goodbye.

Gargoyle, ever the social creature, seemingly has their office buried in the proverbial guts of the Galatia Academy research tracts. 

Your station map informs you that you will need to pass through multiple restricted sections on your journey, and politely suggests that reaching your destination may be infeasible without the proper clearance. 

Despite this warning the journey is mostly uneventful. You suspect guards convey a sense of importance, legitimacy or perhaps carry the implication that you are with the Hegemony Ministry of Technology Standards. Regardless of the reason, you pass without complaint from the Academicians and campus security, within a few minutes you find yourself at the door to Gargoyle's office.

You motion to knock on the door, intending to perform a rhythmic pattern known to all spacers that can carry long distances with minimal exertion. 

The moment before your hand connects with the metal of the actuated door it slides open, revealing the impish face of Gargoyle and causing your hand to flail pathetically against nothing.

"Captain!" Gargoyle whines, "you left me waiting so long! Is that how you treat someone on a first date? And I even brought you flowers." 

"Its okay, I forgive you. Come in, come in! We wouldn't want salacious rumours to spread, would we Captain!"

options: jdp_penroseGargoyleReturnAlone:"You asked me to leave you alone!"

text:
Gargoyle laughs, "that I did! And then you went and believed my sob story! Didn't Arroyo tell you anything about me Captain?" they wave one of their hands. "If I give you any pushback, if I throw a tantrum, you're supposed to give it back to me Captain!" 

Gargoyle stares forlornly, resting chin on hands. "My methods are wasted on you, $playerFirstName. I'm trying, I really am, but it seems you've lost the art of negotiation. Poor, poor Captain, I wonder how long a major player can last without that." 

They continue in a rhyming cadence, "its gone, so sad, gone for good, too bad."

"Do they now?" Gargoyle smiles in a way that feels distinctly predatory, this was ammunition you should not have given them, "you did go on your friend-date after all! Captain I'm so, so, sorry for for propositioning you, please forgive me. I didn't realise you were taken! You'll make a lovely couple I'm sure," they laugh at their own joke for longer than you consider to be strictly necessary.

"I haven't seen from Alviss in a while, he's fun, but too easy." they stop, thinking. "Maybe I should go say hello, might be a nice palette cleanser after cracking the greatest puzzle known to mankind!"

"Yes Captain $playerFirstName, I have the data," the Hacker confirms, "crypto fully cracked, like an egg, delicious yolk extracted right there," they point to a secure datacore on the floor next to their chair.

"It fried some of my implants but I got it done, it was a glorious challenge!" you didn't notice until Gargoyle pointed it out, but some of their dermal implants have been replaced with what you recognise to be older models. 

Gargoyle shrugs at your balking expression, "that's not important, I won't charge you. Now! Lets talk about the results."

Gargoyle bows, "I proudly present. Drum-roll please-" a dramatic flick of their wrist causes speakers around the room to start up, building tension. 

"I just can't wait! Ooooh this is so fun!" Gargiyle bounces from foot to foot, failing to contain their excitement "Ladies, gentlemen and those like myself, I am thrilled to bring you-" they pause for effect. "The Penrose-class Tesseron Fleetkiller!" with a snap of their fingers a holo-projection fills the room, detailed blueprints for the Penrose. "Courtesy of our friends at Omega Godship Dynamics Limited."

Gargoyle smiles, satisfied with the dramatic flair they supplied, "you're dealing with some incredible stuff, Captain $playerFirstName, I have no idea what substance this is, let alone how you would get this much of it."

The hacker drops the act entirely, "I thought as much," comes deadpan, "you just became much more interesting Captain, much more interesting indeed." 

They mime sealing their lips, "nobody will hear about this from me. Although I am keeping a copy-" they notice your expression and quickly move on. "Oooooh look at this!" Gargoyle gesticulates wildly. To your eyes they move randomly, but the computer interprets the motion and enhances part of the holo-projection, enlarging it so that a room of the ship appears overlaid on Gargoyle's office. 

The architecture is strange and unnatural, the walls jagged and harsh, but at least this confirms the ship has an interior to explore at all.

Gargoyle looks smug, "weren't coached on this huh? Well, Captain, let me elucidate. I cracked into a Tachie data-vault a few cycles ago, very easy, I don't think they even knew it was there," Gargoyle rolls their head back, "it was very dull. But useful!" 

"Found lots of very interesting diagrams on their drone fleet in there, and what I saw makes me very interested in this little guy," the hacker points to a holographic object behind them, "that, my dear Captain, is an AI Core Cradlle. If whatever Omega is has a soul, it lives in that room."
